analysis.title: CIO View: Hedge funds
key_insights: September was a weak month for risk assets: global equities fell 1.1% and global bonds fell 1.6% on rising yields, persistent inflation and renewed geopolitical tension. The average hedge fund lost about 1% (HFR estimate).
Less directional strategies held up better. Equity market neutral gained 0.3% and relative value fell 0.9%. Equity hedge fell 1.8% and event driven fell 1.6%.
Trend-following CTAs gained 3.7% on established trends in rates and energy, while discretionary macro lost 1.8%. Results among discretionary managers differed widely by positioning.

Equity long/short managers were hurt by weak broad equities and sharp intra-month reversals in crowded AI and momentum positions. Morgan Stanley prime brokerage data show better stock selection, especially on the short side, but not enough to offset losses on net longs.

US hedge fund net leverage fell to around 45% by mid-October, the lowest since May 2025, after managers rebuilt exposure in September. Gross leverage remains light. AI-related names still make up about 40% of US net exposure, which leaves portfolios exposed to further AI weakness.
Concentrated short positions in smaller, lower-quality companies could amplify volatility if market sentiment improves.

Merger arbitrage fell only 0.3%. US deal value is up 28% y/y through September (UBS IB) and European activity hit a quarterly record in 3Q26. Median US merger spreads narrowed from 1.2% to 0.7% during the third quarter because of a smaller investable deal universe and more competition.

Credit arbitrage fell 1.2% and distressed/restructuring fell 1.7% on rising yields, wider credit spreads and technical selling. UBS says the sell-off did not reflect broad deterioration in credit fundamentals. Senior secured claims and short hedged credit were relatively resilient.

Relative value fell 0.9%. Market neutral fixed income relative value managers held up, while directional rates managers lost on synchronized central bank tightening. French sovereign dislocations and position unwinds pressured swap spread trades, including in the US.

Convertible arbitrage fell 1.8% on higher yields, wider credit spreads and lower equity volatility, especially for AI-linked issuers. September issuance was USD 26.9bn and YTD issuance is a record USD 203.8bn (BofA estimates). Structured credit was resilient, with asset-backed managers down 0.2% and CLOs positive.

Discretionary macro losses came from receiver positions in Europe and the UK, long gold and some equity themes (industrials, mining). Managers positioned for higher rates gained. The pattern resembled the March rates sell-off, with smaller losses. Managers have since taken profits on rate shorts and cut US dollar shorts and long gold.

UBS preferences: low-net and market neutral equity hedge, merger arbitrage, fixed income relative value, discretionary macro, and multi-strategy platforms as a core allocation. It is neutral on directional equity hedge and balanced on distressed, credit arbitrage, convertible arbitrage, structured credit and CTAs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Equities fell on higher yields and geopolitical tension, though AI and semiconductor stocks held up overall.
Resilient activity, heavy sovereign issuance and AI financing needs pushed yields higher.
Middle East tensions lifted energy prices while precious metals declined and the US dollar strengthened.

macro_indicators.reading: Rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, ECB and Bank of Japan
macro_indicators.interpretation: The hikes reinforced expectations of tighter monetary policy.

risk_factors: Further AI-related weakness, given AI is about 40% of US hedge fund net exposure.
Crowded consensus trades in equity long/short, with risk of sharp reversals or squeezes.
Funding and liquidity tightening could force deleveraging and amplify losses in crowded trades.
Low credit spreads limit alpha in credit strategies and reduce the buffer against sudden widening.
Treasury market microstructure dysfunction or a funding squeeze.
Rising office CMBS delinquencies and longer duration securitized exposures.

tension_points.bull_case: Lighter overall positioning leaves room to rebuild exposure if sentiment improves, and AI and semiconductor stocks remained resilient overall in September.
tension_points.bear_case: AI is still about 40% of US hedge fund net exposure, so portfolios are vulnerable to further AI-related weakness despite lower leverage.

theme_stances.key_argument: High dispersion, low correlations and effective short books help low-net and market neutral managers navigate shifting market leadership.
theme_stances.evidence: We hold a preference for low net and market neutral managers

theme_stances.key_argument: Discretionary macro has the flexibility to navigate monetary policy and geopolitical shifts, while CTAs face trend reversal risk.
theme_stances.evidence: We prefer discretionary macro, with its flexible approach

theme_stances.key_argument: A constructive M&A backdrop and deal-specific complexity support the opportunity set where spreads compensate for deal risk.
theme_stances.evidence: We favor merger arbitrage, where a constructive M&A backdrop
